A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same categorical in-context-learning research despite substantial changes to the title, architecture and scope. All 16 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including their appendices, equations and visual results, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original synthetic-data experiments, kernel comparisons and ImageNet classification results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendices F and K report original synthetic and ImageNet experiments, learned-parameter analyses, language generations and GPT-4o evaluations.

M1.justification: V1 directly updates categorical probabilities through a Taylor approximation. V2 introduces learned category embeddings, latent-function scratch space, an expectation-erasure head and cross-attention that recomputes expected embeddings. It also introduces an output softmax, changes Transformer training from squared error to cross-entropy, and develops positional-input language models with optional feed-forward layers.

E1.justification: V2 adds language generation trained on Tiny Stories and Children Stories, extending beyond v1's synthetic classification and ImageNet coverage. It also introduces RBF-anchor synthetic tasks, while retaining a revised quadrant-based synthetic experiment in Appendix F and retaining ImageNet.

E2.justification: V1's ImageNet comparison evaluates linear and softmax GD attention. V2 introduces a linear-probing comparator trained separately for each test context. Its new language experiments evaluate a single-layer Transformer following Radford et al.'s architecture against GD models. The synthetic GD-versus-Trained-TF comparison remains.

E3.justification: Synthetic evaluation changes from probability MSE over 10,000 contexts to Top-1 accuracy and negative log-likelihood over 2,048 test contexts, with revised training-set and context sizes. ImageNet changes from three classes and 30 contextual images to five classes and 50 images, retaining the 900/100 class split. Language evaluation introduces a 256-token window and GPT-4o grading averaged over 200 story completions.

E4.justification: V2 adds training-set-size comparisons, systematic depth experiments up to six attention blocks, learned-weight and matrix-product diagnostics in Appendix F, and feed-forward ablations and generation failure examples. V1's explicit head-count/bias and variable-context-length experiments are absent. These changes substantially revise the questions tested about mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: Five-initialization reporting remains, but v2 explicitly reports synthetic error bars in Figures 2–3 and five-run results for both GD and Trained TF in Appendix F. V1 explicitly specified five initializations for synthetic Trained TF and showed ImageNet seed variability. This refines uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in runs for matched experiments.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced under revised synthetic and ImageNet settings, and language results are added. V1 reports poor Laplacian Trained TF behavior in Appendix C; v2 Figure 6 reports agreement with GD on its revised synthetic data. V2 Figure 5 adds overall GPT-4o scores of 3.62 for softmax GD, 4.84 with feed-forward, 5.04 for the Transformer and 8.11 for true endings. These are new or replaced findings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the Taylor-based categorical derivation with embedding-based functional updates, adds a multiple-kernel formulation, and presents stationary-point Theorems 1–2 with a substantial proof. New assumptions restrict attention parameters, covariate distributions and latent functions. However, Appendix I's recurrence in Eq. (53) omits the residual function term required by Eq. (51), leaving an inconsistency in the new proof.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes empirical evidence for approximate categorical GD and claims a first real-world demonstration using ImageNet. V2 claims an exact multi-step architecture, a stationary-point characterization encompassing softmax attention, and Transformer-comparable language generation with fewer parameters when feed-forward layers are added. The first-real-world-demonstration claim is removed.

C2.justification: V1 emphasizes approximation, small-context bias effects and normalization-related stability. V2 adds interpretations of learned matrices as evidence of GD, attributes much of the language-quality gap to the feed-forward component, and discusses positional-only attention, zero initialization and repetitive generation as limitations. Section 5 also interprets stationary-point existence as suggesting convergence to GD, which is stronger than existence alone establishes.

D1.justification: V2 supplies extensive architecture matrices, synthetic-generation rules, initialization details, language-model dimensions, a Children Stories access link and the GPT-4o evaluation prompts. Conversely, v1's explicit Adam/batch-size disclosures and software-release promise disappear. Both report a 16 GB V100 GPU; neither supplied PDF establishes a released code repository.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work around categorical token embeddings, exact attention constructions and language generation. It adds language-model and evaluation literature including Radford, Eldan and Li, Touvron, and Xiong, plus representer-theorem support. V1's explicit distinction from Hypertransformer's categorical model-generation approach is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, with new contribution and related-work subsections. The narrative now separates model setup, architecture, learning, theory and experiments; the earlier real-valued discussion largely moves to Appendix G. The appendices are reorganized into A–K with a navigation summary, and the title and author list change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and substantially rebuilds the visual presentation. It adds an architecture diagram, depth and accuracy/loss panels, learned-weight heatmaps, language-score tables presented as figures, generation tables and evaluation-prompt figures. Quadrant probability maps are revised, while v1's head-count and context-length displays disappear.

improvement.justification: V2's learned-weight diagnostics, language experiments and feed-forward controls substantially strengthen v1's mainly prediction-based mechanism evidence. However, the central new theoretical guarantee has unresolved problems: Appendix I's Eq. (53) does not preserve Eq. (51)'s residual update, and Section 5 suggests convergence from stationary-point existence. The PDFs do not resolve whether repairing these issues would alter the principal claims. These theoretical concerns prevent a reliable net judgment despite the substantial empirical gains.
